source: NCERT Class XII, Fundamentals of Human Geography, Ch. 3 (Population Composition).

sections.heading: 1. Population Composition
points: **Population composition** = the structure of a population by **age, sex, literacy, occupation, religion, language, rural/urban** residence.
It reveals the character and needs of a society.

sections.heading: 2. Age-Sex Structure and the Population Pyramid
points: **Sex ratio** = number of females per 1000 males (or males per 100 females in some countries); affected by births, deaths, migration.
**Age structure** = proportion in different age groups (children 0–14, working 15–59, aged 60+).

The **population pyramid** shows age-sex structure: a **broad-based (expanding)** pyramid = high birth rate (young population, e.g. Nigeria); a **narrow-based (contracting)** = low birth rate (ageing, e.g. Japan); a **bell/stable** shape = stationary.

sections.heading: 3. Rural-Urban and Occupational Structure
points: **Rural-urban composition** — the share living in villages vs towns; urbanisation rises with development.
**Occupational structure** — division into **primary (agriculture), secondary (industry), tertiary (services)** workers; developed countries have more in tertiary.
**Literacy rate** reflects social development.

sections.heading: 4. Dependency and Development Link
points: **Dependency ratio** = ratio of dependents (children + aged) to the working-age population — high in young/ageing societies.
A large **working-age population** can give a **'demographic dividend'** (as in India).
Composition guides planning (schools, jobs, health, pensions).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Composition = age, sex, literacy, occupation, residence.
Sex ratio = females per 1000 males (in India).
Population pyramid: broad base = expanding (young); narrow base = contracting (ageing).
Occupational structure: primary, secondary, tertiary.
Demographic dividend = a large working-age population.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: A **broad-based (wide) population pyramid = high birth rate/young population** (expanding).
A **narrow base = low birth rate/ageing population**.
**Sex ratio in India = females per 1000 males**.
**Dependency ratio** compares dependents to the **working-age** population.
